feedback: Written before this candidate has raced. The evidence is iteration 0 and iteration 1 in the development simulator (60 trials each). Every run ended off track with progress of 0.10 to 0.15 and one line-loss event. max_error sat at about 0.062 m, just above the 0.06 m limit. Raising kp and ki (iteration 1) changed almost nothing, so the failure is not a gain problem. Steering oscillation stayed low (0.07 to 0.15), so the robot is not weaving. This candidate tests two hypotheses at once: that the outer sensors at x = ±0.03 m are too close to the edge (H2), and that base_speed 1.6 is too fast for bend entries (H3). The sensor argument is weaker than the rationale states. With a 12 mm footprint, the x = 0.03 sensor should still see tape out to roughly 0.048 m offset, so the blind zone before the 0.06 m limit is about 12 mm, not 17 mm. Widening to ±0.04 is still reasonable, but it is not guaranteed to fix the failure. The base_speed drop from 1.6 to 1.3 is the stronger lever, but the candidate changes both fields together, so the next race will not show which one helped. The design is valid, the gains are unchanged from the best raced design (iteration 1, score 49.79), and this is early exploration with nine iterations left. The race is the most useful next step. Read the next telemetry this way: if progress rises clearly above 0.15 on the oval and s-bend and line_loss_events falls, the sensor span or the speed change helped. If progress stays near 0.11 to 0.15, speed is the more likely cause, so lower base_speed further. If the failure moves to a different point on the course, the cause is elsewhere, and the sensors and gains should be revisited.
requested_changes: If progress stays near 0.11 to 0.15 with the wider span, keep the sensors at ±0.04 m and lower base_speed to about 1.0 (the rationale's own next step). This isolates speed as the cause of the bend-entry failure.
If the robot still leaves the line at the same course point with line_loss_events of 1, revert the outer sensors to ±0.03 m and change only base_speed, to test H3 on its own.
If progress rises but completion_time is near 3 s without finishing, keep base_speed at 1.3 and try raising it back toward 1.5 with the wider sensors, since the first goal is staying on the line.
